bullets.title: NVDA: Premarket rally as market bets administration backs Jensen; ASEAN shipment halt is key risk
bullets.body: NVDA stabilized in premarket (SMH +4.45%, NVDA/ANT +3%) as markets anticipate Jensen Huang's upcoming Congressional testimony will be supportive. However, NVDA has quietly terminated server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia following BIS export controls — Malaysia alone had a >10GW data center plan with >50% serving Chinese hyperscalers, creating a material 2H27 upstream supply risk. Chinese firms also reportedly used NVDA Blackwell hardware (GB300/GB200) as collateral for ~190M yuan in Shanghai loans, briefly softening E-Mini futures at 6:44am.

bullets.title: NVDA/TSM/MU: US export controls tighten — TSMC/Samsung halt <16nm Chinese shipments; DRAM & NAND forecasts cut
bullets.body: TSMC and Samsung halted shipments of <16nm products designed by Chinese firms under new US restrictions. TrendForce revised 2027 NAND revenue to $419.3B (29% YoY) and DRAM revenue to $1.15T (69% YoY), with 2027 supply/demand tight (DRAM -3.8%, NAND -3.3%) but contract price gains narrowing in 2H27. NAND ASPs expected to decline 20-25% YoY in 4Q27; conventional DRAM prices forecast to fall broadly from 1Q28, with bear case >15% QoQ declines.

bullets.title: AMD, CRM: Erste Group downgrades both to Hold from Buy; SPOT upgraded to Buy
bullets.body: Erste Group analyst Hans Engel cut AMD and CRM to Hold from Buy, and upgraded SPOT to Buy from Hold. No price targets disclosed. This is a tier-2 house but directionally confirms recent underperformance concerns for AMD and CRM amid slower AI monetization.

bullets.title: CRM: JPM reiterates OW ahead of F3Q27; F4Q cRPO guide of 12%+ key to re-rating thesis
bullets.body: JPM expects F3Q organic cRPO growth ~11% (vs ~10% guide) and a F4Q guide of at least 12% CC, implying ~10%+ organic growth and 2H re-acceleration. Agentforce ARR at $1.5B; premium mix grew to 5% of base from 1% in F1Q25 (each 1% migration = ~$100M revenue). Shares at 10x EV/uFCF on FY27, with re-rating potential on acceleration.

bullets.title: MRVL, MDB, CRM: Upcoming earnings catalysts in first week of December
bullets.body: MongoDB (Tue Dec 1 AMC, consensus EPS $1.61, rev $762.5M), Marvell Technology (Tue Dec 1 16:30 ET, EPS $1.10, rev $3.15B), and Salesforce (Wed Dec 2 AMC, EPS $3.45, rev $11.46B) all report next week. RH reports Thu Dec 3 (EPS $0.69, rev $932.5M unconfirmed).

bullets.title: HUBS: Argus Research downgrades to Hold from Buy on valuation
bullets.body: Argus analyst Joseph Bonner cut HubSpot to Hold from Buy at current price of $210.21, citing valuation concerns. No revised price target disclosed.

bullets.title: COHR, LITE: Optical/transceiver names surge 8%+ premarket on AI infrastructure momentum
bullets.body: Coherent (COHR) +8.1% and Lumentum (LITE) +7.9% in premarket, leading semis-adjacent infrastructure plays alongside broader SMH +4.45% move. No specific catalysts beyond AI infrastructure sentiment and relief rally.

bullets.title: DIS: Secures TRO pausing FCC review of ABC broadcast licenses
bullets.body: Disney obtained a temporary restraining order halting the FCC's early review of ABC broadcast-station licenses, buying time in the regulatory process. No financial impact quantified.

bullets.title: META: Refused to share 'Muse' product for UK Financial Watchdog testing
bullets.body: META declined to provide its Muse product for testing by the UK financial regulator, adding to European regulatory friction. No further financial details disclosed.

bullets.title: AAPL: Holiday smartphone demand solid; iPhone and Samsung tied at 42% share in Citi survey
bullets.body: Citi's US holiday electronics survey shows spending flat YoY but resilient, with iPhones and Samsung Galaxy tied at 42% each for purchase intent. Gaming hardware/peripherals ranked #2 at 44% interest (above TVs), driven by GTA VI anticipation. Foldable interest at 22% with 44% considering future adoption.

bullets.title: TSLA: Optimus China supply-chain index down 5% WoW despite TSLA +10%; FSD V15 launched
bullets.body: Tesla's Optimus China Value Chain Index fell 5% WoW even as TSLA shares gained 10% WoW and the Global Robotics Index rose 4%. Tesla launched FSD V15 with claimed 25x improvement in critical intervention rate. Near-term catalysts: Humanoids Summit Dec 1-2, TSLA Annual Shareholder Meeting Dec 3. Goldman identifies TSLA as 'most balanced robotics platform' but rates it Neutral, preferring XPeng and Toyota.

bullets.title: VRT: Citi maintains Buy/$585 PT despite FDA delay pushing povetacicept approval to Feb 2027
bullets.body: FDA requested additional information late in PDUFA review, delaying Vertex's povetacicept IgAN approval from Nov 30 to Feb 28, 2027. Citi views delay as not thesis-changing but expects near-term stock pressure. Buy rating maintained with $585 PT vs $564.12 current (~3.7% upside). Drug's dual BAFF/APRIL mechanism seen as differentiated.

bullets.title: Piper Sandler: Stay patient on semis; SPX 7,350-7,400 is key confirmation level
bullets.body: Piper Sandler notes major averages remain below 50- and 200-day MAs with intermediate-term breadth on sell signals. Semiconductors flagged as 'remain patient on.' A decisive close above 7,350-7,400 SPX would confirm durable low targeting 7,507; break below 7,002 reopens 6,882. Favor Healthcare/Financials on pullbacks.

bullets.title: Macro bear flag: McCullough warns semis/QQQ bounce is exit liquidity; VXN at 36
bullets.body: Keith McCullough (Hedgeye) warns the China National Team-driven bounce in semis and QQQ is an 'exit liquidity trap,' noting US stocks down 9 of last 10 trading days. VXN at 36 with vol-of-vol risk range 30-46; describes regime as 'chasers get crushed.' SP500 risk range 6,907-7,352. Turning bullish long-term Treasuries into Q4 2026/H1 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA/AI chips: Congress export-control push stalls; Kioxia/NVDA testing SSD as HBM alternative
bullets.body: Congressional efforts to tighten AI chip export controls are facing roadblocks from slow legislative pace and turf battles. Meanwhile, NVDA and Kioxia are testing SSD-based AI server memory as an alternative to South Korean HBM chips, with Kioxia's GP2 SSD targeting 18M+ IOPS (2x prior gen) and 28GB/s sequential reads; evaluation samples to limited customers by end of 2027.
